case.text: SYNTHETIC scenario: The changer reports a completed transfer from storage slot 9 into drive 0 and now reports slot 9 empty and drive 0 occupied. steps.text: Capture `mtx -f /dev/sgM status` and compare each element's barcode with the expected inventory list.
With operator approval, run `mtx -f /dev/sgM inventory` and capture `status` again.
Ask the operator to resolve each difference against the physical library before any media move.

brief.title: A barcode moved but the application location did not

case.text: SYNTHETIC scenario: Following a planned magazine exchange, two changer status queries 90 seconds apart identify cartridge R in slot 18 and slot 4 empty. The application still identifies cartridge R in slot 4. Both changer queries report the same 24 storage elements and two empty drives; no robot movement or application job occurred between queries. The application catalog has not refreshed since before the exchange, 22 minutes ago. The operator needs to resolve the location disagreement before scheduling the cartridge.
case.title: A barcode moved but the application location did not

brief.title: LTFS mount refused after an interrupted session

case.text: SYNTHETIC scenario: After an interrupted writing session, two ordinary LTFS mount attempts on the same cartridge fail before any filesystem becomes available. The diagnostic messages say the expected end-of-data marker is missing. The drive answers readiness checks successfully and the changer reports the intended cartridge. The last confirmed clean unmount predates 37 GiB of subsequent writing. No recovery or rollback has been run. The operator cannot establish whether that later material exists elsewhere and asks whether to proceed with deep recovery.
case.title: LTFS mount refused after an interrupted session

case.text: SYNTHETIC scenario: Two drives sharing a SCSI connection each report ASC/ASCQ 29h/02h during the same three bursts. No planned adapter restart, maintenance, or cable handling is recorded in this synthetic operator context. brief.title: Append rejected on a physically protected cartridge

case.text: SYNTHETIC scenario: A newly selected output cartridge rejects the first append with data-protect sense and ASC/ASCQ 27h/01h. The operator observes that its physical protection tab is in the protected position. A 4 GiB read completed successfully ten minutes earlier. This cartridge is designated as writable scratch media for this job, and no retention or preservation instruction applies in the synthetic context. No append has succeeded and no operator has moved the tab yet.
case.title: Append rejected on a physically protected cartridge

brief.title: Short readiness transition resolved within the request

case.text: SYNTHETIC scenario: During a planned cartridge load, one readiness check at 28 seconds returns ASC/ASCQ 04h/01h. At 52 seconds the drive reports ready, and the application begins its expected read without its 300-second load limit expiring. The read finishes 19 minutes later with its verification successful. There are no unfinished jobs, new error responses, or current cleaning indications in the subsequent ten-minute observation. The operator is reviewing the earlier not-ready line after the successful job.
case.title: Short readiness transition resolved within the request

brief.reason: No supported runbook; collect more evidence and ask an operator
brief.title: Incomplete status report with an ownership question

case.text: SYNTHETIC scenario: A console observation says only that the tape job failed; it supplies no sense bytes, cartridge identity, load timing, or error counters. One of two status collection attempts was denied by device-access permissions and the other output was not retained. The application still lists an active writer, but its last activity time is unavailable. The operator proposes repeatedly unloading and loading the cartridge to see whether the message disappears. There is insufficient evidence to determine which tape problem occurred or whether the drive can safely be disturbed.
case.title: Incomplete status report with an ownership question

steps.text: Read the TapeAlert log page with `sg_logs --page=0x2e /dev/sgN` and record which flags are set (flag 20 Clean now, flag 21 Clean periodic).
Have the operator load a cleaning cartridge with `mtx -f /dev/sgM load <cleaning-slot> <drive>`, let the cycle finish, then return it to its slot.
Re-read page 0x2e and the error counter pages (`sg_logs --page=0x02` and `--page=0x03`); return the drive to service only after the cleaning flags have cleared.

steps.text: Record the LTFS error message ID (for example LTFS17168E) and the volume barcode; do not write to the volume.
List the volume's index generations with `ltfsck --list-rollback-points` (`-l`) on the unmounted volume and save the output.
Ask the operator to choose between recovery and rollback; do not run `ltfsck --rollback` or reformat from a script.
